title: Most Adults Cannot Pass This Surgeon's Entrance Exam
summary: Explore surgical knowledge through clues, practical situations and fresh challenges.

landing.intro:
Precision starts with knowledge.
How well can you connect the clues?

about.body: Connect the facts, notice the details and test your understanding of surgical knowledge. Each checkpoint reveals your topic profile before a different challenge begins.

steps: Read the clues and choose one answer.
See your topic profile at each checkpoint and continue to a new challenge.
Reveal your overall result, then optionally review the answers you missed.

about.disclaimer: For entertainment and general learning only. This is not a medical-school admission exam, surgical qualification, diagnosis or medical advice. Seek qualified medical care for personal symptoms, wound concerns or emergencies.

surgeon-s1q1.question: Which gas does blood pick up in the lungs?

surgeon-s2q1.question: In anatomical position, what does medial mean?

surgeon-s2q2.question: What does proximal mean when describing a limb?

answers.a3: Closer to its attachment to the body

surgeon-s2q4.question: Which membrane lines much of the abdominal cavity?

surgeon-s2q5.question: What carries blood away from the heart?

surgeon-s2q6.question: What is the mesentery associated with?

answers.a1: Supporting parts of the intestine and carrying vessels and nerves
answers.a2: Covering the outside of the skull
answers.a4: Separating the chambers of the heart

surgeon-s2q7.question: Which term means closer to the body’s surface?

surgeon-s3q2.question: What is the purpose of a suture?

surgeon-s3q3.question: What does a surgical retractor do?

answers.a4: Holds tissue aside to improve access or visibility

surgeon-s3q5.question: What does laparoscopic surgery typically use?

answers.a2: Small incisions and a camera to view the operative area
answers.a3: Sound waves as the only cutting instrument

surgeon-s4q1.question: Hands are visibly dirty. Which cleaning method is appropriate?

answers.a1: Put gloves on over the dirt

surgeon-s4q2.question: What should happen after protective gloves are removed?

answers.a3: Keep the gloves for another person
answers.a4: Clean hands only if a glove tore

surgeon-s4q3.question: Which container is designed for used needles and other sharps?

answers.a3: An open tray for later sorting

surgeon-s4q4.question: A task may splash body fluid toward the face. Which protection addresses that risk?

surgeon-s4q5.question: Shared observation equipment has been used. What should happen before reuse?

answers.a1: Use it unchanged if it looks shiny
answers.a2: Cover old marks with a label
answers.a4: Clean it using the approved method

surgeon-s4q6.question: A sterile package is torn before use. What is the safe conclusion?

answers.a1: The printed date cancels the tear
answers.a2: The contents are sterile if they look clean

surgeon-s4q7.question: Which statement about protective gloves is correct?

answers.a1: They do not replace hand hygiene
answers.a2: The same pair is suitable for every patient
answers.a3: They stay clean regardless of what they touch

surgeon-s5q1.question: Before surgery, why confirm the patient, procedure and intended site together?

answers.a1: To prevent wrong-patient, wrong-procedure or wrong-site errors
answers.a3: To decide the patient’s favourite colour
answers.a4: To replace every other safety check

surgeon-s5q2.question: What is the purpose of a surgical team pause before an incision?

answers.a1: To let one person guess the whole plan
answers.a2: To stop communication during the operation

surgeon-s5q3.question: Why should team members know one another’s names and roles?

surgeon-s5q4.question: An instrument count does not match the expected count. What should happen?

answers.a1: The discrepancy must be resolved using the safety procedure
answers.a2: Change the expected count without checking
answers.a3: Ignore the count if everyone is busy
answers.a4: Assume the missing item was never present

surgeon-s5q5.question: Why label a tissue specimen with verified identifying details?

answers.a1: To predict the diagnosis from the handwriting
answers.a2: To connect the specimen with the correct patient and site
answers.a3: To remove the need for laboratory examination

surgeon-s5q6.question: A team member notices a possible safety problem. What supports safer teamwork?

surgeon-s5q7.question: What belongs in a postoperative handover?

answers.a1: An assurance that monitoring is never needed
answers.a2: Relevant procedure details, concerns and the agreed recovery plan
answers.a3: Only the length of the operation

surgeon-s6q1.question: What is a main early role of a blood clot at a wound?

answers.a2: Limiting blood loss and forming a temporary seal

surgeon-s6q2.question: Which protein is important in the structural strength of healing tissue?

surgeon-s6q3.question: What does inflammation bring to an injured area?

answers.a1: Only new bone cells in every tissue
answers.a2: A guarantee that infection is present
answers.a3: Immune cells and changes in local blood flow
answers.a4: Permanent loss of every blood vessel

surgeon-s6q4.question: Why can inadequate blood supply impair healing?

answers.a1: Wounds heal only when completely dry internally
An unchanged piece of original tooth enamel
answers.a3: Repair tissue rich in fibrous connective material
answers.a4: A pocket of air in every wound

surgeon-s6q7.question: Why does wound healing take more than one moment?

answers.a1: Healing is only a change in skin colour
answers.a2: Every wound follows an identical clock
answers.a3: Several overlapping biological processes must occur
answers.a4: Cells can repair tissue only once a year

surgeon-s7q1.question: A person says, “I’m worried about what happens next.” What is the best opening?

answers.a1: Promise there is no possible risk
answers.a3: Acknowledge the worry and invite questions

surgeon-s7q2.question: Someone wants to discuss a sensitive concern in a busy public area. What protects privacy?

answers.a2: Write the details on a public board

surgeon-s7q3.question: A person has not understood an explanation. What helps check understanding?

answers.a1: Explain plainly and ask them to describe it in their own words
answers.a2: Ask another patient to answer for them
answers.a3: Treat a nod as proof of understanding

surgeon-s7q4.question: Before a non-urgent examination, what should the person receive?

answers.a1: Only a form with no explanation
answers.a2: A clear explanation and an opportunity to consent
answers.a3: An assurance that questions are not allowed
answers.a4: A decision made by the nearest visitor

surgeon-s7q5.question: A person declines having students present. What is the respectful response?

answers.a3: Assume silence later cancels the choice
answers.a4: Respect the choice and protect privacy

surgeon-s7q6.question: A language barrier makes an important discussion difficult. What is the best support?

answers.a3: Asking a young child to interpret sensitive details

surgeon-s7q7.question: A person with hearing difficulty asks you to repeat yourself. What is helpful?

answers.a3: Face them and check their preferred way to communicate

surgeon-s8q1.question: A record shows 800 mL plus 250 mL. What is the total?

surgeon-s8q2.question: How many millilitres are in 1.5 L?

surgeon-s8q3.question: How much time passes from 09:20 to 10:05?

surgeon-s8q4.question: You count 9 breaths in 30 seconds. What is the equivalent rate per minute?

surgeon-s8q5.question: A recorded total rises from 600 mL to 900 mL. What is the percentage increase?

surgeon-s8q6.question: Divide 1.2 L equally across four recorded periods. How much belongs to each?

surgeon-s8q7.question: Three sealed boxes hold eight items each. How many items are there?

surgeon-s9q1.question: A pulse changes from 72 to 88 beats per minute. What does the record show?

answers.a2: An increase of 16 beats per minute
answers.a3: A decrease of 16 beats per minute
answers.a4: An increase of 8 beats per minute

surgeon-s9q2.question: Earlier, a person spoke comfortably. Now they pause between short phrases to breathe. What changed?

answers.a2: The record proves a specific diagnosis

surgeon-s9q3.question: Which observation describes a new change in alertness?

answers.a1: The chart has a new page
answers.a4: The room lights were switched on

surgeon-s9q4.question: Which description records a breathing rate?

surgeon-s9q5.question: What does a pulse oximeter estimate?

surgeon-s9q6.question: Why should a reassuring device reading not replace assessment of new symptoms?

answers.a1: One number proves all body systems are healthy
answers.a3: Every device always gives random values
answers.a4: Measurements have limitations and need context

surgeon-s9q7.question: Which change calls for prompt qualified assessment?

answers.a2: New breathing difficulty with reduced alertness
answers.a4: A different pen used for notes

surgeon-s10q3.question: A fasting instruction conflicts with another instruction in the record. What is the safest response?

answers.a1: Clarify the instructions with the responsible team
answers.a3: Follow the shorter instruction without checking

answers.a2: To prove everyone heals at the same rate
answers.a3: To understand the person’s needs and guide the care plan
answers.a4: To assume silence always means no pain

surgeon-s10q5.question: A recovering patient develops new breathing difficulty. What is needed?

answers.a2: Waiting for a routine appointment without reporting it
answers.a3: Prompt assessment by the appropriate clinical team

surgeon-s10q6.question: Why include mobility and activity instructions in discharge information?

answers.a2: Recovery needs vary with the person and procedure
answers.a3: Activity has no relationship to recovery
answers.a4: Every operation has the same recovery plan

surgeon-s10q7.question: Which discharge explanation best checks understanding?

answers.a1: Ask them not to ask questions
answers.a3: Ask the person to explain the plan and when to seek help
